what: Arrives fast and settles gently. The default for things entering.
ask: ease out the boxes as they arrive
live: c.P(t0, d, kit.ease.out)

what: Starts slow and leaves fast. Good for things falling or leaving.
ask: let the runs ease in as they drop
live: c.P(t0, d, kit.ease.in)

what: Goes slightly past its mark and settles back. Adds snap and weight.
ask: overshoot the crown when it jumps
live: c.P(t0, d, kit.ease.back)

what: Items enter one after another, not all at once, so the eye can count them.
ask: stagger the seven rungs
live: kit.stagger(t0, i, gap)

what: Appears by scaling up with a small bounce. For new items worth noticing.
ask: pop each log entry in
live: kit.ease.back on size

what: Stops on a frame so the viewer can read it before anything moves again.
ask: hold on the ladder for a beat
live: a narration hold (narration.json holds) or a gap between movements

what: Fades in while sliding a short way. The plain way to bring in text.
ask: reveal the subtitle after the title
live: op: c.P(t0, d) with a small y offset

what: A line or outline draws itself, so the eye follows its path.
ask: draw on the iceberg outline
live: S.path(key, d, {p}) / S.line(..., {p})

what: A fill sweeps across, like a brush stroke. Says 'all of these, the same way'.
ask: wipe the four colours on in one stroke
live: a width driven by c.P

what: One shape becomes the next. The diagram is rebuilt, not replaced, so you see what changed.
ask: morph the machine into the three replicas
live: lerp each rect's x, y, w, h by c.P

what: The shape that ends one moment is where the next begins, so a change of idea still feels continuous.
ask: match cut from memory to the snapshot
live: same key, new position and label

what: The camera moves closer to one detail. Says 'look here'.
ask: push in on the ladder at the end
live: c.camAt([[t0, {x, y, z: 1}], [t1, {x, y, z: 2}, 'heavy']]); in 3D, a smaller span: c.shot([[t0, s], [t1, {...s, span: s.span / 2}, 'heavy']])

what: The camera retreats to show the whole picture again, after a push-in or to reveal where a detail sits.
ask: pull back to the whole map once the record is saved
live: c.camAt([[t0, close], [t1, {x: W / 2, y: H / 2, z: 1}]]); in 3D, a larger span

what: The camera slides to another part of the picture at the same zoom. Says 'now over here', and keeps the way between the two places visible.
ask: pan to the database
live: c.camAt([[t0, {x: x1, y, z}], [t1, {x: x2, y, z}]]); in 3D, the shot's target moves

what: The camera moves and zooms so a group of things just fills the picture, below the header and above the captions.
ask: frame on the three replicas
live: c.camAt([[t0, here], [t1, c.frameOn([x0, y0, x1, y1])]]); in 3D, c.shot([[t0, here], [t1, c.frameOn3(points, {az, el, fov})]])

what: A label joined to its subject by a thin leader line.
ask: callout the hot level
live: S.callout(key, x, y, tx, ty, text, p)

what: A line crosses out an idea as it is dismissed. Shows what was tried and why it lost.
ask: strike through each problem as the next stage fixes it
live: S.strike(key, x1, x2, y, p)

what: A brief swell to draw the eye, then back to normal.
ask: pulse the crown when it moves
live: kit.pulse(t, t0, d)

what: A quick bright overlay that marks an instant: a snapshot, a power cut.
ask: flash when the snapshot is taken
live: a white rect with op kit.pulse(...)

what: A kick on a heavy hit: smooth noise scaled by the square of its trauma, gone in half a second, at most 12 px and 1°.
ask: shake the frame when the platter lands
live: shake(kit, t, t0, trauma) from templates/live/scenes/example-feel.js

what: A heavy contact held for 2 to 6 frames, then catching up, so the hit has weight.
ask: hitstop the strike for three frames
live: hitstop(t, t0, frames, fps) from templates/live/scenes/example-feel.js, with "hitstop" on the cue

what: A number ticks to its value, so you feel the size of it.
ask: count up the rebuild time
live: kit.countUp(t, t0, d, a, b, fmt)

what: Everything but the subject fades back, so focus moves without a cut.
ask: dim the rest while the primary fails
live: lower op on the others by c.P

what: Separate things slide into one and soften into a single blend. Says 'these are no longer separate'.
ask: blur the four colours together
live: S.blur(id, sd) as the filter, positions lerped together

what: A value passes set points at set times, each leg with its own ease. For a path with stops on it.
ask: keyframe the crate: up, across, then down heavy
live: kit.keyed(t, [[t0, a], [t1, b, 'out'], [t2, c, 'heavy']])

what: Slow to get going, then decisive, landing with a firm stop. Gives weight to big things and conclusions.
ask: bring the verdict down heavy
live: c.P(t0, d, kit.ease.heavy)

what: The gentlest ease in and out, an even sway with no sharp change. For drifting, ambient moves that shouldn't call for attention.
ask: float the clouds across
live: c.P(t0, d, kit.ease.float)

what: Arrives fast and stops dead, with no bounce. For things clicking into place.
ask: snap each tile into the grid
live: c.P(t0, d, kit.ease.snap)

what: A part trails what it hangs on: it starts late, swings past and catches up. Secondary motion that makes a move feel physical.
ask: give the tag some follow-through when the box moves
live: kit.follow(t, s => xAt(s), lag)

what: After a stop it rocks a few times, smaller each time, then rests. Shows the landing had force.
ask: let the sign settle after it lands
live: y + kit.settle(t, tLand, amp)

what: A small drift that never visibly repeats, like a hand-held camera. Keeps a held frame alive without moving anything.
ask: add a slight wobble to the hanging lamp
live: x + kit.wobble(t, amp, freq, seed)

what: The camera circles the subject at the same distance, so you see how its parts sit behind each other. For showing depth, not for decoration.
ask: orbit round the stack once it opens

what: The camera rises or dips round the subject: from straight above, a plan, to an angle that shows height.
ask: tilt down so the layers show

what: A flat diagram turns into the 3D thing it draws: seen from straight above it matches the diagram exactly, then the camera tilts and perspective opens.
ask: open the platter into depth on 'tilt it'
live: draw the SVG diagram until t0, then c.shot([[t0, c.flatShot()], [t1, tilted, 'heavy']]) with the 3D model in the same coordinates

what: The camera returns to straight above and perspective closes, and the flat diagram takes over again with what changed.
ask: flatten it back to the diagram at the end
live: c.shot([[t0, tilted], [t1, c.flatShot(), 'heavy']]), then the SVG diagram from t1

what: An assembly comes apart along its axes so every part shows, in order, and closes again the same way.
ask: explode the stack so each platter shows
live: each part's offset along its axis from kit.keyed(t, [[t0, 0], [t1, gap, 'heavy']])

what: A label on the stage joined to a point on a 3D part: it rides with the camera and stays upright and readable.
ask: label the heads while the camera turns
live: const [x, y] = c.G.project(point); S.callout(key, x + dx, y + dy, x, y, text, p)
